classification_reasons: The overall change adds a new Bash/PowerShell authorization hook (shell_guard.py) exercised on every shell call in every phase plus a sandbox.filesystem.denyWrite layer in CI, touches sdlc.yaml risk_list item 'auth', and went through many fix rounds closing successive bypasses before being accepted - not a tight, small-blast-radius routine change.

This round's own diff (the git -C composition fix and its test, plus the already-verified as_posix() test fix) is small and self-contained, but it does not change the surrounding change's classification.
attempted: Intent: the round stays inside intent.md's authz problem - it corrects a real gap in the already-approved shell_guard.py hook (a chained `git -C a -C b` was resolved against the wrong base directory), not a new or adjacent feature.

Spec/plan: plugin/hooks/shell_guard.py and tests/test_hooks.py are already listed in plan.md's Files that change; the fix stays inside spec.md Design's already-approved cwd/cd-chain resolution rule (following a literal cd/pushd/Set-Location/git -C). This matches the precedent of this same change's many earlier hardening rounds (e.g. round 4's 21 items), none of which required a plan.md edit for an internal parsing-correctness fix to an already-planned file; no open Flagged concern reopened.

Proof: independently re-derived the bug and the fix rather than taking the account on trust. Read _git_global_scan in plugin/hooks/shell_guard.py directly: before this round it kept only the last `-C` value seen (`dash_c = value`), so `git -C sub -C ..` resolved against `cwd/..` instead of against `cwd/sub/..`; outside the project root, protected_paths._check_one's rel_to() returns None and the write is allowed even though real git's own -C composition resolves back onto the project root. The fix, `dash_c = value if dash_c is None else str(Path(dash_c)/value)`, composes successive -C values the way git does; the later norm()/fs_path() call (posixpath.normpath) lexically collapses the resulting '..' before the protected-pattern match, so the composed path correctly re-resolves onto the root. Verified the new test test_shell_guard_composes_chained_git_dash_c_targets exercises both directions: `git -C sub -C .. rm CLAUDE.md` from the project root must block (and does, by the traced logic), and `git -C sub -C . rm CLAUDE.md` must stay allowed (and does). Also re-checked the sibling test_shell_guard_git_dash_c_does_not_leak_into_a_later_chain_part is unaffected (it only exercises the no-persistence-across-chain-parts rule, not composition) and that the single, non-chained `-C` tests (test_shell_guard_resolves_a_git_dash_c_target, test_shell_guard_sees_a_dash_c_preceded_by_another_global_option) still pass under the new code (dash_c starts None, so the ternary degrades to the old behaviour for a single -C). Confirmed the previously-reported Windows-path fix (review #5489774399) is actually present in the current file: the three tests now call project.as_posix()/other.as_posix() inside the f-string Bash commands, with no assertion changed.

evidence/test.log, build.log and lint.log read '# <command> - deferred to the runner' lines timestamped at this session; per this project's CI convention (plugin 0.3.2 item 3b) this is not missing proof - the runner replaces them after the session, so judged the diff and the code directly instead of these logs.
evidence/review-findings.json's head matches current HEAD (7764e7a) and reports 0 Important/0 nits from a fresh pass; used as corroboration only, not as the basis for my own verdict.

Blast radius: this round's own diff is confined to plugin/hooks/shell_guard.py (one function) and tests/test_hooks.py (one new test); no guardrail file, no change to the sandbox/CI settings, no change to risk_list beyond the already owner-accepted 'auth' item; test-file lock does not engage (change_type: feature).

Policies: checked the new test lines for the security-baseline scanner's three DANGEROUS literals (eval(, exec(, shell=True) - none present; no credential in the diff; coding-standards rule 4 (tests not weakened) - the new test is additive, and the Windows-path fix changes only how a path is interpolated into a command string, not any assertion.

Tests: traced whether the composed-dash_c fix could still pass with the bug present - it could not, because the old single-value overwrite is structurally different from the new Path-join composition and the new test's back_to_root case directly exercises the composed, cross-directory '..' case the old code mishandled; also checked no pre-existing test was weakened to make this pass (the diff to this file in the cumulative patch is purely additive at this hunk, @@ -1756,3 +1756,696 @@, confirming no existing assertion was touched).
